parsed.name: ai_power_global
parsed.strategy: Bet that the AI capex bottleneck sits in physical power, not chips: grid transformers, switchgear, cables, turbines, liquid cooling and the HBM that feeds the racks. Every name has a dated observable inside Oct 12-Nov 13 (GEV/NVT/VRT prints, ASML Oct 14, TSMC Oct 15, SK Hynix/Samsung late Oct, Hon Hai Tech Day Oct 30-31, Cameco Nov 3-4, Siemens Energy and Korean grid names mid-Nov). I would be wrong if a hyperscaler capex digestion headline, a China export-control shock, or a de-escalation-driven risk-premium compression hits the whole chain at once, since these names are highly correlated to one AI-power factor.
parsed.objective: Maximize relative P&L vs the Bloomberg WLS index from 2026-10-12 to 2026-11-13 with a long-only global AI power and memory book.

strategy.brief: AI power bottleneck, worldwide: power generation, grid, cooling, transformers, turbines and the memory that AI capex buys. Prefer names with a dated observable (backlog, orders, earnings) in the window. Competition rules: long only, global, <= 10% per name, >= 8 names, NO ETFs, cash <= 2%, graded as relative P&L vs the Bloomberg WLS index from 2026-10-12 to 2026-11-13.
